## Data Wrangling: 

```{r}
# Combining all surveys from different years all together (adding more years) 
#Ghana: 
allyears_ghana <- suppressWarnings(bind_rows(ghana_2008, ghana_2022))

allyears_ghana

#India

allyears_india <- suppressWarnings(bind_rows(india_2005, india_2015, india_2020))


#Nigeria 
all_years_nigeria <- suppressWarnings(bind_rows(nigeria_2008, nigeria_2013, nigeria_2018, nigeria_2024))

#Kenya

all_years_kenya <- suppressWarnings(bind_rows(kenya_2008, kenya_2014, kenya_2022))



```



/
/
/
##Merging Datasets: 

```{r}
#Combining all datasets for ALL years survey for all countries.
combined_dhs<- suppressWarnings(bind_rows(allyears_ghana, allyears_india, all_years_nigeria, all_years_kenya))  %>% 
  filter(v044 == 1) #Filtering for women age 15-49 selected and interviewed for the domestic violence module

head(combined_dhs_2)
nrow(combined_dhs_2)
ncol(combined_dhs_2)
```


The dataset has 362588 observations of women between 15-49 who were interviewed on the GBV module from 4 countries (India, Kenya, Ghana, Nigeria) and 65 variables of interest. 

```{r}
#Wrangling new dataset: 


#Creating new variable names: 
combined_dhs_2<- combined_dhs%>%
  mutate(
  reported_to_family =
    as.integer(rowSums(across(d119a:d119r), na.rm = TRUE) > 0),

  reported_to_friend =
    as.integer(rowSums(across(c(d119s, d119t, d119xd)), na.rm = TRUE) > 0),

  reported_to_other =
    as.integer(rowSums(across(c(d119xa, d119x)), na.rm = TRUE) > 0),

  reported_to_cs_organisation =
    as.integer(rowSums(across(c(d119xc, d119xi, d119xj, d119xk)), na.rm = TRUE) > 0)
) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    c( d119u, d119xb, d119xf, d119w, d119xe, d119xg, d119xh, d119v),
    ~ as.integer(replace_na(.x, 0) > 0)
  )) %>% 
  mutate(across(c(d119y, d118y), ~ as.integer(replace_na(.x, 1) == 1))) %>%  
  rename(
    "caseid" = caseid,
    "current age - respondent" = v012,
    "ever-married sample" = v020,
    "literacy" = v155,
    "ever participated in a literacy program outside of primary" = v156,
    "highest educational level" = v106,
    "highest year of education" = v107,
    "education in single years" = v133,
    "educational attainment" = v149,
    "wealth index" = v190,
    "wealth index factor score (5 decimals)" = v191,
    "type of place of residence v025" = v025,
    "type of place of residence v024" = v024,
    "type of place of residence v102" = v102,
    "number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)" = v137,
    "Ever been threatened with harm by husband/partner" = d103b,
    "Experienced any less severe violence" = d106,
    "Experienced any severe violence" = d107,
    "Previous husband: ever hit, slap, kick, or physically hurt respondent" = d130a,
    "Respondent was not hurt by anyone during a pregnancy" = d118y,
    "No person other than husband/partner ever physically hurt respondent" = d115y,
    "Experienced any sexual violence" = d108,
    "Previous husband/partner: physically forced to have sex or to perform sexual acts" = d130b,
    "Ever forced to have sex by anyone other than husband/partner in last 12 months" = d124,
    "Ever forced to perform unwanted sexual acts" = d125,
    "Have ever told anyone else about violence" = d128,
    "Respondent did not seek help from anyone" = d119y,
    "reported_to_neighbour" = d119u,
    "reported_to_Social_service_organisation" = d119xb,
    "reported_to_Religious_leader" = d119xf,
    "reported_to_Employer" = d119w,
    "reported_to_Police" = d119xe,
    "reported_to_Criminal_Justice_System" = d119xg,
    "reported_to_Public_health_official" = d119xh,
    "reported_to_Public_education" = d119v, 
    "Country" = Country, 
    "Year" = Year
  ) %>% 
  select(-(starts_with("d119")))  %>% 
  #Creating GBV variable
  mutate(
    experienced_GBV = if_else(
      # Condition: either any GBV variable >= 1
      rowSums(across(c(
        `Ever been threatened with harm by husband/partner`,
        `Experienced any less severe violence`,
        `Experienced any severe violence`,
        `Experienced any sexual violence`,
        `Previous husband: ever hit, slap, kick, or physically hurt respondent`,
        `Previous husband/partner: physically forced to have sex or to perform sexual acts`,
        `Ever forced to have sex by anyone other than husband/partner in last 12 months`,
        `Ever forced to perform unwanted sexual acts`
      ), ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0
      # OR if either of the "no violence" indicators is 0
      | replace_na(`No person other than husband/partner ever physically hurt respondent`, 1) == 0
      | replace_na(`Respondent was not hurt by anyone during a pregnancy`, 1) == 0,
      1,  # value if TRUE
      0   # value if FALSE
    )) %>%
  mutate(`education in single years` = if_else(`education in single years` == 99,NA, `education in single years`)) %>%
  mutate(`ever participated in a literacy program outside of primary` = if_else(`ever participated in a literacy program outside of primary` == 9,NA, `ever participated in a literacy program outside of primary`)) %>% 
  mutate(`educational attainment` = if_else(`educational attainment` == 9, NA, `education in single years`))


summary(combined_dhs_2$`wealth index factor score (5 decimals)`) #How is it measured : PCA 
summary(combined_dhs_2$`wealth index`) #How is it measured? : A categorical variable of 1-5
summary(combined_dhs_2$`education in single years`) #on a x -y scale of schooling, hower it is country specific 
summary(combined_dhs_2$`ever participated in a literacy program outside of primary`)
summary(combined_dhs_2$`type of place of residence v025`)
summary(combined_dhs_2$`number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)`)
```
Wealth index factor: measured using principal components analysis (PCA), Households below the average on the combined assets/amenities will have negative scores. Households above the average will have positive scores. (higher number richer households and lower scores poorer households )

Education in single years: A measure of education on x and y axis (x the level, and y the specific grade, however, it is country specific)

```{r}
library(scales)

# Summarize data by Country and Reported_GBV
bar_graph_2 <- combined_dhs_2 %>%
  filter(experienced_GBV == 1) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`Respondent did not seek help from anyone`)) %>%
  mutate(
    Report_GBV = `Respondent did not seek help from anyone` == 0,
    Reported_GBV = if_else(Report_GBV, "Reported", "Did not report")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Country, Reported_GBV) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n))  # calculate proportion for stacked bar

# Plot 100% stacked bar chart
ggplot(bar_graph_2, aes(x = Country, y = pct, fill = Reported_GBV)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(data = filter(bar_graph_2, Reported_GBV == "Reported"),
            aes(label = paste0(round(pct*100), "%")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Reported" = "red", "Did not report" = "darkred")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage of Self-Initiated GBV Reporting by Country, 2005–2024",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Experienced GBV",
    fill = "Reported GBV"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
  
```

#GBV prevalence in sample: 
According to the UN definition, which guided the identifcation of experienced GBV variable, According to all our samples the percentage of women who are randomaly sampled who have experienced gender based violence is 25%. So 1 in 4 women, had been Ever been threatened with harm by husband/partner,Experienced any less severe violence, Experienced any severe violence, Experienced any sexual violence, Previous husband: ever hit, slap, kick, or physically hurt respondent, Previous husband/partner: physically forced to have sex or to perform sexual acts, Ever forced to have sex by anyone other than husband/partner in last 12 months.Ever forced to perform unwanted sexual acts. Overall showing that GBV is pretty prevalent. 

Though the prevalence rates vary significantly accross countries, there seems to be a high count of GBV in Kenya with what appears as almost half of the sample (precisely 51%),have experienced and then Nigeria (34%) and India (19%)

However when we look at the graph we can see that even less, report GBV, as it is comparatively lower have reported to their experience. To examine the disparity in reporting we can see that in this graph, where reported is constantly lower than experienced. 

However there are country specific differences among the survey responses: There is a very low reporting rate in india and nigeria, but there seems to be an equal amount of reporting and no reporting relative to those who experience GBV. 





```{r}
#As I started my analysis: Only state and non state: 

#Creating dataset for 2 different reporting modes: 
Data_with_2_reporting_modes <- combined_dhs_2 %>% 
  mutate(state_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(reported_to_Police,reported_to_Criminal_Justice_System, reported_to_Public_health_official, reported_to_Public_education),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) %>%
  mutate(non_state_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(reported_to_Social_service_organisation, reported_to_Religious_leader, reported_to_cs_organisation, reported_to_Employer, reported_to_neighbour, reported_to_family, reported_to_friend, reported_to_other),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    ))
#Summary stats of 
Reporting_proportion<- Data_with_2_reporting_modes %>%
   filter(experienced_GBV == 1) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_experienced = n(),
    total_reported = sum(`Respondent did not seek help from anyone` == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_reported_state =  sum(state_reporting == 1, na.rm = TRUE), #How many of those reported went to state 
    total_reported_non_state = sum(non_state_reporting == 1, na.rm = TRUE)  #How many of those reported went to non-state
  )

Reporting_proportion

```

```{r}
#Descriptive stats table for #2 modes.
#First table: 
Reporting_proportion_2<- Data_with_2_reporting_modes %>%
   filter(experienced_GBV == 1) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_experienced = n(),
    total_reported = sum(`Respondent did not seek help from anyone` == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_reported = 100 * (sum(`Respondent did not seek help from anyone` == 0, na.rm = TRUE)/total_experienced),
    total_reported_state = sum(state_reporting == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_reported_state = 100 * (sum(state_reporting == 1, na.rm = TRUE)/ total_experienced), #How many of those reported went to state
    total_reported_non_state = sum(non_state_reporting == 1, na.rm = TRUE), #How many of those reported went to non-state
    pct_reported_non_state = 100 * (sum(non_state_reporting == 1, na.rm = TRUE)/ total_experienced)
)

Reporting_proportion_2


#1st table on total surveyed per country :

#3rd Table: Combining both + Wrangling 
descriptive_stats_2modes <- left_join(Total_sample, Reporting_proportion_2, by = "Country" ) %>%

descriptive_stats_2modes

```

```{r}
#Creating final descriptive stats table: 

#final Descriptive statistics table. 
# Step 1: Add info rows
long_table_2 <- descriptive_stats_2modes %>%
  select(Country,
         total_surveyed, pct_surveyed,
         total_experienced, pct_experienced, 
         total_reported, pct_reported,
         total_reported_state, pct_reported_state,
         total_reported_non_state, pct_reported_non_state
         ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Country,
    names_to = c(".value", "Measurement"),
    names_pattern = "(total|pct)_(.*)"
  ) %>%
  # Combine count and percent
  mutate(Value = paste0(total, " | ", round(pct, 2))) %>%
  select(Country, Measurement, Value)

# Add informational rows
info_rows <- tibble(
  Measurement = c("base_surveyed", "base_reported"),
  Country = rep(NA_character_, 2),
  Value = rep(NA_character_, 2)
)

long_table_2 <- bind_rows(
  long_table_2 %>% filter(Measurement == "surveyed"),
  info_rows[1,],  # info before experienced
  long_table_2 %>% filter(Measurement == "experienced"),
  info_rows[2,],  # info before reported to state
  long_table_2 %>% filter(Measurement == "reported"),
  long_table_2 %>% filter(Measurement == "reported_state"),
  long_table_2 %>% filter(Measurement == "reported_non_state")
)

# Step 2: Pivot wider
wide_table_2modes <- long_table_2 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Country, values_from = Value) %>%
  # Rename Measurement for readability
  mutate(Measurement = recode(Measurement,
                              surveyed = "Survey Participation",
                              experienced = "Experienced GBV",
                              reported = "Reported GBV to someone",
                              reported_state = "Reported To State",
                              reported_non_state = "Reported To Non-State",
                              reported_social_circle = "Reported To Social Circle",
                              base_surveyed = "Base =  per country survey participation",
                              base_reported = "Base = having experienced GBV"))


wide_table_2modes

```

There seems to be overalap, let's see how many only responded to each and how many reported to both. 
```{r}
Exclusive_Reporting <-  Data_with_2_reporting_modes %>%
  filter(experienced_GBV == 1) %>%
  mutate(
    report_type = case_when(
      state_reporting == 1 & non_state_reporting == 0 ~ "Reported Only State",
      state_reporting == 0 & non_state_reporting == 1 ~ "Reported Only Non-State",
      state_reporting == 1 & non_state_reporting == 1 ~ "Reported Both"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Country, report_type) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

#Summary stats of the general exclusive reporting. 
Exclusive_Reporting_summary <- Exclusive_Reporting %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = report_type, values_from = Count, values_fill = 0)

#Pie chart of the exclusive reporting of survey.
Exclusive_Reporting_proportion<- Exclusive_Reporting %>%
group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(Proportion = Count / sum(Count))


ggplot(Exclusive_Reporting_proportion, aes(x = "", y = Proportion, fill = report_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 1.5) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  facet_wrap(~ Country) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "purple", "pink", "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Exclusive Reporting Categories of GBV by Country",
    fill = "Report Type"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 14)
```
```{r}

Exclusive_Reporting <-  Data_with_2_reporting_modes %>%
  filter(experienced_GBV == 1) %>%
  mutate(report_type = case_when(
      state_reporting == 1 & non_state_reporting == 1 ~ "Reported Both",
      state_reporting == 1 & non_state_reporting == 0 ~ "Reported Only State",
      state_reporting == 0 & non_state_reporting == 1 ~ "Reported Only Non-State")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(report_type)) %>% 
  mutate(
    report_type = fct_relevel(report_type, 
                              "Reported Only Non-State",
                              "Reported Both",
                              "Reported Only State")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Country, report_type) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(pct = Count / sum(Count))




ggplot(Exclusive_Reporting, aes(x = Country, y = pct, fill = report_type)) +
 geom_col(position = "fill") + 
geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct*100), "%")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white") +
   scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Reported Only Non-State" = "#F4A6C1",  # light pink
      "Reported Both" = "#E85A8C",            # medium pink
      "Reported Only State" = "#CC2F4D"       # deep pink-red
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Exclusive GBV Reporting Choices",
    fill = "Reporting Choice",
  y = "%") +
  theme_minimal()

```


After evaluating the distribution, we can see that the majority of non-state reporting is less about social organisations and NGOs and more about family and friends, hence we proceed to further disegregate the data, into 3 reporting modes. 

```{r}
#Creating variables for different reporting modes: 

Data_with_3_reporting_modes <- combined_dhs_2 %>%

                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) %>%
  mutate(non_state_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(reported_to_Social_service_organisation, reported_to_Religious_leader, reported_to_cs_organisation, reported_to_Employer),

      1, 0
    )) %>% 
  mutate(social_circle_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(reported_to_neighbour, reported_to_family, reported_to_friend, reported_to_other),

      1, 0
    ))

Data_with_3_reporting_modes
```


##BINOMIAL REGRESSIONS : 
#For both 2 reporting modes (state and non-state) and 3 reporting modes (state, non-state and social circle): 

#A logistic regression for state reporting: 

```{r}
#A logistic regression for state reporting fiex effects on country
library(fixest)

state_reporting_model <- feglm(
  state_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + 
                    `Respondent did not seek help from anyone`  + 
                     `current age - respondent` +
                     `educational attainment` + 
                     `wealth index factor score (5 decimals)` + 
                      `type of place of residence v025` +
                     `number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)`,
  data = Data_with_2_reporting_modes,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  fixef = "Country"   # fixed effect for country
)
summary(state_reporting_model)

```



```{r}
#Check for multicollinearity. 
library(car)
vif(state_reporting_model)
```
Change the interpretation: 

The fixed-effects logistic regression examining reporting to state-affiliated mechanisms indicates that participation in a literacy program outside of primary school increases the odds of reporting by about 8.8% (OR = 1.088, p < 0.01).However it seems that each additional year of education is associated with a 5.4% decrease in the odds of reporting (OR = 0.946, p < 0.01). Household wealth is positively related to reporting: a one-unit increase in the wealth index corresponds to a very small but statistically significant increase in the odds of reporting (OR ≈ 1.000003, p < 0.01). Overall, these results suggest that both educational experiences and socio-economic status influence the likelihood of engaging with state reporting mechanisms, even after accounting for country-level differences.

#A logistic regression for non-state reporting: 

```{r}
non_state_reporting_model <- feglm(
  non_state_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + 
                    `Respondent did not seek help from anyone`  + 
                     `current age - respondent` +
                     `educational attainment` + 
                     `wealth index factor score (5 decimals)` + 
                      `type of place of residence v025` +
                     `number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)`,
  data = Data_with_2_reporting_modes,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  fixef = "Country"   # fixed effect for country
)
summary(non_state_reporting_model)
```
*Change interpretation: 

In the regression predicting reporting GBV to non-state actors, women living in rural areas (v025 = 2) had odds of reporting about 64% higher compared with urban women (p ≈ 0.062), indicating a marginally significant effect. Additionally, each additional child under five in the household was associated with odds of reporting about 40% higher (p ≈ 0.011).


## using 3 reporting types: 
```{r}
#State there was no change 
state_reporting_model_2 <- feglm(
  state_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + 
                    `Respondent did not seek help from anyone`  + 
                     `current age - respondent` +
                     `educational attainment` + 
                     `wealth index factor score (5 decimals)` + 
                      `type of place of residence v025` +
                     `number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)`,
  data = Data_with_3_reporting_modes,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  fixef = "Country"   # fixed effect for country
)
summary(state_reporting_model_2) #No change 


```
```{r}
#Specifically looking in social organisation and community organisations. 
non_state_reporting_model_2<- feglm(
  non_state_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + 
                    `Respondent did not seek help from anyone`  + 
                     `current age - respondent` +
                     `educational attainment` + 
                     `wealth index factor score (5 decimals)` + 
                      `type of place of residence v025` +
                     `number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)`,
  data = Data_with_3_reporting_modes,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  fixef = "Country"   # fixed effect for country
)
summary(non_state_reporting_model_2)
```
In the regression predicting reporting of GBV to NGOs and social organizations, each additional year of education was associated with about a 6.6% decrease in the odds of reporting (p ≈ 0.001), suggesting that more educated women were slightly less likely to turn to NGOs for reporting. Women who had ever participated in a literacy program outside of primary school had approximately 6% higher odds of reporting to NGOs and social organizations, though this effect was marginally significant (p ≈ 0.056). The wealth index factor score, which ranges roughly from –2,440,200 to 2,626,500 in this dataset, had a very small positive coefficient per unit (0.00000189), indicating that a one-unit increase barely changes the odds. However, considering the full range of the wealth index, the difference between the poorest and wealthiest households could translate to a substantial cumulative effect on reporting behavior (p ≈ 0.081). Women living in rural areas had roughly 21% higher odds of reporting to NGOs and social organizations compared with urban women, with this effect marginally significant (p ≈ 0.080). Overall, these findings suggest that rural residence and prior literacy program participation may modestly increase the likelihood of using non-state social avenues for reporting, whereas higher formal education slightly decreases it, and wealth may have a small cumulative influence across its full scale. 


```{r}
#Specifically looking in social circle reporting 
social_circle_reporting_model<- feglm(
  social_circle_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + 
                    `Respondent did not seek help from anyone`  + 
                     `current age - respondent` +
                     `educational attainment` + 
                     `wealth index factor score (5 decimals)` + 
                      `type of place of residence v025` +
                     `number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)`,
  data = Data_with_3_reporting_modes,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  fixef = "Country"   # fixed effect for country
)
summary(social_circle_reporting_model)
```
In the regression predicting reporting of GBV to a respondent’s social circle, age and the number of young children in the household were significant factors. Each additional year of age was associated with a decrease in the odds of reporting to one’s social circle by about 3.5% (p ≈ 0.0001), indicating that older women were less likely to share experiences of GBV with friends or family. Conversely, each additional child under five in the household was associated with an increase in the odds of reporting to the social circle by approximately 30% (p ≈ 0.0038), suggesting that women with more young children were more likely to turn to their immediate social networks for support. These findings highlight how age and caregiving responsibilities influence non-state, informal reporting behaviors.

## Data reporting looking at 3 modes of reporting (State, non-state reporting and social circles): 
##Multuvariate logitical regression

Using multivariate logistic regression because it me model these three outcomes jointly, accounting for potential correlations between them.Especially as these outcomes are not independent—for example, someone who reports to a social circle may as well to report to the state or social organisations. 
```{r}
Data_with_3_reporting_modes<- Data_with_reporting_variable %>% 
  mutate(state_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(d119xe,d119xg, d119xh),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) %>%
  mutate(non_state_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(d119xb,d119xf),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) %>% 
  mutate(social_circle_reporting = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(d119a:d119y),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    ))
```


```{r, eval = FALSE}
#Fitting a multivariate logistic regression:  
library(brms)
model <- brm(
  bf(state_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + Reported_GBV + v012 + v020 + v155 + v156 + v106 + v107 + v133 + v149 + v190 + v191 + v025 + v024 + v102 + v137, family = bernoulli()) +
    
  bf(non_state_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + Reported_GBV + v012 + v020 + v155 + v156 + v106 + v107 + v133 + v149 + v190 + v191 + v025 + v024 + v102 + v137, family = bernoulli()) +
    
  bf(social_circle_reporting ~ experienced_GBV + Reported_GBV + v012 + v020 + v155 + v156 + v106 + v107 + v133 + v149 + v190 + v191 + v025 + v024 + v102 + v137, family = bernoulli()),
  data = Data_with_3_reporting_modes,
  chains = 4, iter = 1000
)

summary(model)
```

statereporting_v137                       0.80      0.54     0.18     1.55 4.55        4       11
A one unit increase in v137 (number of children 5 and under in household (de jure)) is associated with 0.8 increase in the log odds of reporting to state.  (around 2.2 fold increase in the odds of reporting). 

nonstatereporting_v020                   -0.96      0.60    -1.71    -0.14 3.95        4       13
v020- ever-married sample being in the ever-married being ever married is associated with  about 38% of the odds for unmarried women.

nonstatereporting_v149                    0.63      0.49     0.14     1.33 4.53        4       11
One unit increase in educational attainment is associated with 0.63 increase in the odds of reporting to non-state. exp(0.63) (nearly 88% higher odds per unit increase in education.)


socialcirclereporting_v155                1.26      0.16     0.98     1.40 4.51        4       11
in being literate is asociated with more than triples the odds of social circle reporting. 

socialcirclereporting_v025               -1.12      0.50    -1.67    -0.47 3.37        4       12
The odds of reporting to the social circle are roughly  exp(-1.12) = 67% lower for that type of residence compared to the reference category—if the estimate were reliable.

however for all the coefficient we  cannot trust their estimate yet because none of the model estimates not converge (Rhat >> 1) and the effective sample sizes are extremely low.

Two profiles of women, mean of age and wealth index, number of children. Odds ratio...

```{r}
      rowSums(across(c(`Ever any emotional violence`, `Experienced any less severe violence`, `Experienced any severe violence`, `Experienced any sexual violence`, `Previous husband: ever hit, slap, kick, or physically hurt respondent`, `Previous husband/partner: physically forced to have sex or to perform sexual acts`, `Ever forced to have sex by anyone other than husband/partner in last 12 months`, `Ever forced to perform unwanted sexual acts`) ,
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) 

GBV_variable %>% 
  count(experienced_GBV)


GBV_variable <- combined_dhs_2 %>% 
  mutate(experienced_GBV = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(d104, d105a:d105n, d110a:d110h, d115b:d115y),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) 

GBV_variable %>% 
  count(experienced_GBV)
```

```{r}
#Creation of reporting  variable
Data_with_reporting_variable <- combined_dhs_2 %>%
  mutate(experienced_GBV = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(d104, d105a:d105n, d110a:d110h, d115b:d115y),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    )) %>% 
  filter(experienced_GBV == 1) %>%
  mutate(Reported_GBV = if_else(
      rowSums(across(c(d119a:d119xk),
                     ~ .x >= 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      1, 0
    ))

head(Data_with_reporting_variable)

Count <- Data_with_reporting_variable %>%
  count(experienced_GBV, Reported_GBV)
Count
```
